desc:
Return the node values of a binary tree in preorder: first the root, then everything in the left subtree (in preorder), then everything in the right subtree (in preorder). The empty tree gives the empty array.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree on the left: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For tree = [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] the answer is [1, 2, 4, 3]. For tree = [1, -1, 2, 3] (root 1, no left child, right child 2 whose left child is 3) the answer is [1, 2, 3].

Try to do it without recursion, using an explicit stack.
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: Preorder means: visit the node first, then go into the left subtree, then into the right subtree.
Recursion is the direct translation. To avoid it, use a stack that holds the nodes still waiting to be visited.
Push the root. Repeat: pop a node, record its value, then push its right child and afterwards its left child, so that the left child is popped first.
editorial: The recursive definition is three lines: record the node, recurse left, recurse right. An iterative version replaces the call stack with your own. Keep a stack of nodes that still have to be visited. Pop one, record it, and push its right child followed by its left child. Because a stack is last-in first-out, the left child comes out before the right one, and the whole left subtree is finished before the right child is touched.

With the level-order array you do not need node objects: the k-th real node's children sit at slots 2k+1 and 2k+2, so you can precompute for every real node the index of its left and right child and run the stack on indices. Every node is pushed and popped once: O(n) time, and the stack never holds more than the tree height plus one entry per pending right sibling, so O(n) space in the worst case.
